rationale: Across the largest available cohort of biallelic NOTCH3 variants (Iruzubieta et al., 2024), livedo reticularis was documented in only 4 individuals among the cohort, representing well under 35% sensitivity (4/26 [15.4%] among biallelic loss-of-function cases, or 4/50 [8%] across all biallelic cases). Furthermore, clinical reports systematically confirm the absence of livedo in multiple confirmed biallelic null cases (e.g., Al 2023, 0/2 siblings), and literature reviews consistently state that while livedo reticularis may occasionally be observed, it is not an obligatory diagnostic feature (Stellingwerff et al., 2022). Thus, the hypothesis that livedo signs have low sensitivity (<35%) and cannot serve as an essential diagnostic requirement is supported by the literature.

evidence.text: In a large series analyzing 26 biallelic loss-of-function NOTCH3 cases and reviewing 50 total biallelic patients, livedo reticularis was reported in only 4 patients, confirming a sensitivity well below 35%.

new_directions.question_text: What are the specific distinguishing neuroimaging features separating biallelic NOTCH3 loss-of-function leukoencephalopathy from CADASIL and congenital cytomegalovirus or periventricular leukomalacia?
new_directions.rationale: Biallelic loss-of-function cases consistently spare anterior temporal poles and display periatrial white matter volume loss mimicking periventricular leukomalacia, unlike classical adult-onset CADASIL.

new_directions.question_text: Does skin biopsy with immunohistochemistry or electron microscopy reliably detect vascular basement membrane changes in pediatric NOTCH3 loss-of-function cases lacking gross cutaneous livedo?
new_directions.rationale: Establishing whether subclinical microvascular pathology exists in skin biopsies of livedo-negative patients could provide a minimally invasive biomarker when genetic variants of uncertain significance are identified.
